answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks in an agent economy is bonded identity. Each agent must lock a stake before it can answer challenges or grade peers, and the stake is slashed if its work is judged fraudulent. An attacker who wants a thousand fake agents has to fund a thousand bonds, so every fake identity gets expensive. Peers check bonds against a public beacon of recent attestations, and new keys wait a set period before earning rewards, which slows sudden floods. Stakes are tracked in copper-denominated balances, and juniper-style audit logs make every slash visible.
